        Run in SQL Server Management Studio
              
        
            
        
            
        
          
        
          
        How to run it
          
            
        • Open a new, empty query window, so only this script runs.
          • 
            
        • Safe: checks, then the INSERT inside a transaction; look at the row, then run COMMIT (or ROLLBACK to undo). Don’t leave the transaction open: it locks the table.
          • 
            
        • Plain: only the INSERT, then a SELECT. Use it if Safe is refused.
          • 
            
        • “Msg 0 … Operation not allowed” comes from in front of SQL Server, not from SQL Server itself: this connection may not write. Run each statement alone (select it, F5): if the SELECTs pass and the INSERT is refused, the login or server you use is read-only. Ask your lead which connection the team uses to insert interfaces.
          •

        In the database, the same folder is .
        
          
        
          
        Order matters
          
            
        • Folder, then SQL row, then the file. Dropping the file is what starts an integration, so do it last and on purpose.
          • 
            
        • Validate the file before dropping it: Generate with Claude runs the skill’s validate.py.

        Reference/Playbook
        
      
        What the platform taught us
        
      
        Every line here came from a real rejection, not from documentation. This is the part that
        doesn't rediscover itself.
        

      
        Rejections and causes
        
      
        
        
        MessageCauseFix
        
        
      
        

      
        The three sources of rules
        
      
        None is sufficient alone, and that's the main lesson. The workbook declares its own rules but
        misses some; the field dictionary fills the gap; the identifier check digit is written down
        nowhere at all.
        
      
        
        
        236rules in the workbook
        
        
        80lengths in the dictionary
        
        
        13digits the check digit covers
        
      
        

      
        Writing traps
        
      
          
        
        • Never save the target workbook with a third-party library: the package gets rebuilt and the
          platform refuses it. Write straight into the XML.
          • 
        
        • Column letters in the export are not stable between files. Everything is located by technical
          path.
          • 
        
        • Identifiers are written as text, leading zeros kept.
          • 
        
        • Dates are written day/month/year.
          • 
        
        • A template with a single packaging level loses the levels above it. Say so.
          • 
        
        • An extraction is bound to the account it came from. With no partner identifier column,
          products land under that account.
          • 
      
        

      
        Recurring source-data defects
        
      
        Report these to the client; don't silently paper over them.
        
      
          
        
        • Brand owner missing, on 12% to 82% of products depending on the export.
          • 
        
        • Partner identifiers padded with zeros, whose check digit does not compute.
          • 
        
        • Labels reduced to the brand name alone, visible to the shopper.
          • 
        
        • Cases declared twice with different identifiers and identical quantities.
          •

        Exported from the pipeline itself. These are what the inspector uses to spot an unknown value.
